Kermeli, K., Deuchler, R., Worrell, E. and Masanet, E. (2016). Energy Efficiency and Cost Saving Opportunities for Metal Casting: An ENERGY STAR Guide for Energy and Plant Managers. Document Number EPA 430-R-16-001, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Office of Air Programs, Climate Protection Partnership Division, January 2016. No DOI or URL printed.

Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 4). All tons are short tons (p.1 footnote 1) and 'MBtu' is million Btu; units are kept as printed (MMBtu/short-ton, kWh/short-ton, Btu/lb of metal). An ENERGY STAR measure catalogue: nearly every number is reprinted from other works (Eppich 2004, Schifo and Radia 2004, BCS 2005, Foundrybench 2011, Kennedy 2001, White 2011 etc.), named in each note. Main file (40 technologies, 45 examples): Appendix B whole-foundry purchased energy by carrier for 5 iron (Table 5), 4 steel (Table 9) and 7 aluminum (Table 10) foundries, named foundry_* and mapped (none); melting furnaces with their own energy or efficiency figures: cupola (efficiency), coreless induction (470 kWh/ton modern, 650-775 typical European, 762 clean-scrap batch melter), steel-foundry electric melting 454-726 kWh/ton, foundry EAF before/after foamy slag (514/465), twin-shell EAF (269), gas-fired, electric resistance and induction crucibles (Btu/lb), reverberatory furnaces (efficiency, dry-hearth, wet-bath, improved, White 2011 radiant-roof upgrade path to recuperative and regenerative burners, electric radiant roof), stack melter, isothermal melting. _measures.csv: quantified measures and case studies of Chapters 11-20 plus the foundry case studies of Chapters 4-5; generic cross-cutting rules of thumb (motors, pumps, lighting, HVAC) not transcribed. _other-values.csv: totals and primary energy of Tables 5, 9, 10, sector statistics, furnace loss shares, the doubtful stack-furnace 600 kWh/ton. Not loaded: Figures 1-2 (chart only), Appendix C diagram (image), heat treatment (the guide gives only its 50-70% share of energy cost, no technology figures), ladle preheating (savings only, in _measures), no capex for whole furnaces is printed. Flows not written (only SEC by carrier). No price year is printed for any cost; measure costs use 2016_USD with the flag.

(1) Table 9: stainless induction foundry natural gas printed 267.2 MBtu/ton but total 49.1 and electricity 22.4 imply 26.7 (loaded as derived). (2) Table 5 totals differ from the sum of carriers for the cupola rows (9.54 vs 9.59; 10.50 vs 10.51; 5.90 vs 5.98). (3) Table 10 totals off by 0.1 for facilities 4 and 5. (4) Appendix tables are numbered Table 1/Figure 1-4 in Appendix A but referred to as Table 4 and Figure 7 in the text. (5) p.79 'the electricity use in stack furnaces is 600 kWh/ton' for gas-fired stack melters (carrier doubtful). (6) p.52-53 holding vessels '10 Btu per ton per hour' vs '30-40 Btu/ton/hour' - implausibly small units. (7) p.69 says 'the coil of an electric arc furnace' in the induction chapter. (8) p.82 lid cooling rate '16.6 to 13.5 degF/foot (12.5 to 6.8 degC/min)' - unit slip and inconsistent conversion. (9) p.60 launder losses '13 degF (2 degC) per foot' and '34 instead of 57 degF (1 instead of 14 degC)' inconsistent conversions. (10) Overview says Chapters Three through Twenty-four but the guide has twenty chapters. (11) Heating-value basis not stated for any table; only Figure 1 footnote 4 says fuel energy contents are HHV.
